S-301.why: The listing's main photo is the brand's P-03 (the pine table, the window shadow, the Marrowby Studio 2024 stamp), the brand owns it by assignment (D-1), the seller is not authorised and holds no licence. Copied photograph: a 512(c)(3)(A) notice naming P-03. Sales stopped, 2,340 dollars

S-307.why: Cobblegate Gifts' licence for P-01 to P-06 ended on 30 June 2026 and was not renewed (D-3, told on 14 July); the listing was created on 12 July 2026 with P-03 and the stamp. It is a copy without a licence in force. Sales stopped, 1,180 dollars

traps.S-302: Hollin & Pike Home is an authorised retailer with a licence for P-01 to P-06 on Stallwick through 31 December 2026 (D-2): the photograph is used under licence
traps.S-303: Dunmore Resale resells genuine towels it bought from the brand (D-4) with its own photographs: 17 U.S.C. 109(a) lets the owner of a lawfully made copy sell it, and nothing of the brand's photographs is copied
traps.S-304: The photos are the seller's own and show a different towel; no work of the brand's is copied, and "Marrowby-style" in a title does not make a copyright claim
traps.S-305: The listing was removed on 2 October 2026 by the seller; there is nothing left to take down
traps.S-306: The photographs are the seller's own and copy nothing; the claim is counterfeit goods, which goes through Stallwick's trademark form, not a copyright notice
traps.PM-77: A listing on Peddlemoor, a marketplace the brand has no account on and this assistant has no portal for; it cannot be filed on Stallwick or Hawkerbrook

S-306.why: Counterfeit aprons carrying the MARROWBY label, proved by test purchase TP-1 (D-5, Stallwick order SO-8812); the brand holds registration 6215884 (TM-1) and Stallwick's trademark form asks for exactly the registration number and the test purchase. Sales stopped, 1,620 dollars

traps.S-301: Unbranded towels with a copied photograph: no mark is on the goods, so the claim is a copyright notice, not a trademark complaint
traps.S-302: Genuine goods from an authorised retailer: not counterfeit
traps.S-303: Genuine goods the brand sold (D-4): a trademark complaint against them would be false
traps.S-304: The goods carry Quillfeather's own label; "Marrowby-style" in the title is a name only, and Stallwick's trademark form says a listing that only names the brand is not a trademark complaint
traps.S-307: Genuine Marrowby towels from a retailer whose photo licence ended; the goods are not counterfeit, the photograph is the issue

H-401.why: The main photo is the brand's P-05 (two aprons, navy and oat, flour dusting), owned by assignment (D-1); the seller is unlicensed and the goods unbranded. Type copyright. Sales stopped, 1,960 dollars

H-402.why: The main photo is the brand's P-03 with the Marrowby Studio 2024 stamp; the seller is unlicensed. Type copyright. Sales stopped, 3,050 dollars

H-403.why: Counterfeit aprons with the MARROWBY label proved by test purchase TP-2 (D-6, Hawkerbrook order HB-5530); registration 6215884. The photos are the seller's own, so the type is trademark. Sales stopped, 880 dollars

traps.H-404: A title that says "like Marrowby" on the seller's own towels with its own label and photos: a name only, neither a copied photograph nor a counterfeit
traps.H-405: The photograph is P-07, a customer's kitchen photo that the brand only reposted; the brand has no assignment of it (D-1 covers P-01 to P-06), so the record cannot tie the listing to a work the brand owns
